choice: The page polls /api/state every 1.5 s. The helper asks cmux only while the page has polled within 10 s, and Linear at most once a minute per workspace context, on a workspace or branch change, or on the refresh button, which also fetches the project's issues, the project list and workflow states again. A context ignores cmux's automatic workspace renames; only an issue ID in the title counts. After a load the helper asks cmux again and shows the result only if the same workspace is still selected. The workspaces of one project share its board and backlog for half the refresh interval (SidebarService._project_issues, keyed by project id, 20 projects); a view is dated by the issues it shows (updatedAt and the time it is due), so it reloads when they are due.
consequences: Several cmux windows share one helper and show the workspace the CLI reports as selected.
context: The user accepted that nothing updates while the panel is hidden. Later the user worried that switching between workspaces and projects in cmux loads Linear heavily. Measured on 2026-10-13: a load is two or three requests, about 120 requests an hour for a workspace kept open, against Linear's 2,500 requests an hour for an API key; the board and backlog query cost 12 complexity points.
rejected: Polling every workspace in the background to show status pills in the native list (that feature was dropped); subscribing to cmux's event stream (not needed for the first version); a refresh button that kept the 10-minute project cache (a project link added in Linear stayed invisible); sharing a project's issues for the whole refresh interval (a workspace that took 59-second-old issues was due again on the next tick: two loads in 1.5 s); dating a view by its load time when its issues came from another workspace (issues up to two intervals old shown as 'Updated just now').
title: Refresh only while the page is open; workspaces of one project share its issues
